item.text: {"text":"“A Framework and Toolkit for Testing the Correctness of Recommendation Algorithms,” by Lien Michiels, Robin Verachtert, Andres Ferraro, Kim Falk and Bart Goethals, appeared in ACM Transactions on Recommender Systems 2(1), Article 4, March **2024**, 45 pages; DOI: 10.1145/3591109. It adapts metamorphic testing, property-based testing and coverage analysis to recommendation algorithms, combining black-box and white-box checks at unit, integration and system levels. Testing RecPack, PyLensKit, Surprise and Cornac uncovered bugs and undocumented requirements despite existing high coverage. [Paper text](https://paperity.org/p/376503724/a-framework-and-toolkit-for-testing-the-correctness-of-recommendation-algorithms).\n\nThe released Python toolkit is **RecPack Tests**; source repository: [recpack-maintainers/recpack-tests](https://gitlab.com/recpack-maintainers/recpack-tests). For this task, useful adaptations of its testing approach—not verified built-in toolkit checks—include comparing trained-model and exported-predictor scores/rankings on identical histories and candidates; checking checkpoint reload parity, candidate-permutation equivariance, batch-versus-single inference consistency, finite outputs and correct category/item routing. Architecture-aware diagnostics should exercise the actual model and scoring path. For causal sequential models, additionally test that changing future tokens cannot affect earlier features; avoid treating history-order invariance as a universal requirement. These checks complement validation HR@10 by detecting implementation faults that aggregate accuracy can conceal."}
